v1.feedback: The crepuscular idea genuinely drives the design — low-angle sun rimming cells in warm amber, god-rays as geometry, ghost cells drifting into darkening sky — and the hiraeth lineage (detaching cells longing away from the body) reads clearly through the twilight filter. Two things to tighten: the god-rays as static triangle fans will read as flat cardboard cutouts at oblique angles; consider a screen-space radial blur from the sun point instead, or at minimum animate their opacity with a noise-driven flicker so they breathe. Second, 20k instanced spheres at r=0.08 risk reading as a granular blob once dense — scale sphere radius down as neighbor count rises so the surface reads as membrane, not buckshot.

v2.feedback: The crepuscular sun (low raking angle, warm amber key + cool fill, god-ray radial blur) is a genuine and well-mapped mutation of the hiraeth parent — the form reads as wr5 after twilight has passed through it, which is exactly the brief. However, the structural behavior (spring physics, detachment age, nutrient rate) appears essentially unchanged from the parent; a stronger chain mutation would let the twilight concept inflect the growth itself — e.g. cells on the sun-facing side could photosynthesize faster while shadow-side cells detach sooner, creating asymmetric dissolution that *is* the crepuscular idea rather than just being lit by it. The god-ray post-pass risks washing out the membrane detail at certain angles; consider clamping its intensity or masking it behind the organism's silhouette so the cellular texture stays readable through the rays.
